title: Ordinary integral open extension and normalized identity-image comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $X$, let $B_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and its inverse-image coefficient identifications be the specified completed coefficient system [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Use the ordinary unbounded categories $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ and ordinary ringed pro-etale module direct image and its total right derived functor [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], define $j_!^{\mathrm{ord}}$ to be termwise exact descent of the completed-coefficient open extension of [def-sp-open-coefficient-adjunction-data].

Define $e_X:(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)}$ to be the unique natural isomorphism whose inverse, for every module sheaf $M$, pro-etale object $V\to X$, and section $x\in M(V)$, sends $x$ to its restriction along the canonical map $V\times_X X\to V$. Here the direct image uses the actual completed coefficient identification for $\mathrm{id}_X$. The section maps are linear and natural because that coefficient identification is the identity-base-change map, and the inverse base-change map supplies their inverses; sections determine module-sheaf morphisms, so this characterization determines $e_X$ uniquely. Let $d_X:R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))}$ be the composite obtained by right deriving $e_X$, comparing the derived identity with the exact termwise identity, and using the canonical identity-descent isomorphism. For the compactification $(j,\mathrm{id}_X)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], define the canonical comparison from the separately derived compact-support image $P_{B,(j,\mathrm{id})}=R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\circ j_!^{\mathrm{ord}}$ [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data] to $j_!^{\mathrm{ord}}$ by whiskering $d_X$ with $j_!^{\mathrm{ord}}$ and then applying the right unitor. These are the existing constructions ordinaryOpen, identityModuleImage_existsUnique, identityModuleImage, identityImage and openIdentity; the normalization is part of the definition, with no assertion about preservation of constructibility or completeness.
